title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers
statement: You are given a list nums of at least two non-negative integers. For every pair of distinct indices i != j, compute nums[i] XOR nums[j]; return the single largest such value as an integer. Equal values sitting at different indices form a valid pair (their XOR is 0), so an answer always exists. The intended approach builds a binary trie: insert each number as a fixed-width bit string of 32 bits, walking from the most significant bit (bit 31) down to the least significant bit (bit 0) and creating a child node for each 0/1 bit. Then, for each number, walk the same trie greedily from bit 31 down, at every level preferring the branch holding the opposite bit (to make that XOR bit a 1) and falling back to the same-bit branch when the opposite branch does not exist. Track the best XOR seen across all numbers and return it. Zero-pad narrow numbers to the full 32-bit width so the most significant differences are always compared first.
hints: Trying all pairs is O(n^2). What structure lets you, for a fixed number, quickly find the stored number whose bits disagree the most with it?

Insert every number into a binary trie, one node per bit, from the most significant bit down. Comparing high bits first matters because a single higher bit outweighs every lower bit combined, so use a fixed 32-bit width and zero-pad.

For each number, descend the trie from bit 31 to bit 0: at each level compute the opposite bit and take that branch if it exists (adding 1<<bit to the running XOR), otherwise take the same-bit branch. Keep the maximum running XOR over all numbers and return it. Never assume the opposite branch exists.
